_anchors.canvas.w: 64. The machine spans 33 px prop to sternpost and the roll never changes its LENGTH — roll is about screen x, so x extents are invariant and the cell needs no flip margin sideways. 15 px of margin either side holds the outline and the bob.
_anchors.canvas.h: 48, and the worst pose is the QUARTER ROLL, not the rest pose: the 30 px top-wing span sweeps into the vertical, reaching 15 px either side of the hull. 30 rows of sweep + wheels at 9 below + outline fits with 2 rows spare; 64 would spend 16 rows on nothing.
_anchors.canvas.originX: 32, dead centre. The hull is near symmetric about its own middle and the sprite never flips (the street games run one way), so centre is the cheapest true answer.
_anchors.canvas.originY: 26. The hull's own axis — the centre of the barrel roll, as the skate put its origin at the hip that the somersault turns about. Wheels reach 9 below (row 35), the quarter-roll wing 13 above (row 13).
_anchors.tones.perMaterial: 5, the 15/08 idiom. Six materials at five tones is 30 entries + transparent.
_anchors.frames.walk: 8, forced by the four named phases of the cruise: the quarter marks must land on frames or src/core/contract.ts refuses the manifest — the ink probe's defect, held off by a lock since.
_anchors.light.x: -0.5, upper left, the shelf's lamp. The dawn in this scene is a BACKDROP fact; the subject keeps the project's key or it disagrees with every other body ever placed beside it.
_anchors.light.y: -0.55, low. A low sun rims the wing edges, and the wing edge is the surface this round has to keep readable at 2 px.
_anchors.light.z: -0.3, toward the viewer, the skate's value: both wing faces have to be legible through the roll and a grazing lamp would lose one.
_anchors.light.curve: 1.1. Slightly above linear; the machine is the bright thing against a dawn sky, so the dark end compresses less than the crypt's 1.3.
_anchors.gait.swing: 0.05 turn = 18° at a key of 1. The largest cruise key is 0.6 on the SCARF (11°, cloth in an airstream); the hull's is 0.14 (2.5°, a trim wobble). DERIVED from what level flight does, not carried from another clip — run 7's recorded lesson.
_anchors.gait.lift: 2 px. The hull bobs ±1 px on the cruise, half the skate's pump: a machine on air moves less than a body on legs.
_anchors.gait.depth: 6 px. Unused; every cruise track is screen-plane or scale.
_anchors.gait.roll: 0, and the zero is the null case for the channel on this subject: if the cruise changes when roll ships, the change came from somewhere it had no business reaching — the skate-roll rule, re-armed for the transfer.
_anchors.body.scale: 1. The machine is 33 px long in a 240 px world — the runner proportion, three obstacles of warning on screen.
_anchors.texture.dither: 0 on the body, and the number is the skate round's measured result carried, not re-derived: a small body has no single-owner surface for a lattice (rider 0.000 at 4×4). The weave in this game lives on the sky and the world below, at full amplitude.
_anchors.texture.lattice: 2, the body value, unused at dither 0.
_anchors.shadow.steps: 7, one more than the deepest mass (the fuselage at 3.2, the wing span treated by its 26 px depth is capped by the solver).
_anchors.shadow.strength: 2 ramp steps, the outdoor value the street uses.
_anchors.fill.y: 0.4, from below — at altitude the fill IS the sky bouncing off the undersides.
_anchors.fill.weight: 0.1, the street's value: enough to keep the cream undersides from going mud, not enough to flatten the wing edge.
_anchors.playback.msPerFrame: 90, read only by the bench: in the game the cruise advances with distance over strideLen, so this number cannot disagree with the world's speed.
_anchors.outline.material: "ink", the skate's blue-cast near-black: the sky behind is warm, so a cool line separates from the scene's light instead of fighting it.
_anchors.outline.inner: true, and Part.weld places it: fabric-on-fabric is one skin (wings, fin, fuselage), everything bolted or strapped keeps its seam (cowl, struts, wheels, pilot, scarf) — the kitten rule.
